title: What happened
goal: Talk about past events — what you did, where you were, what happened — using the simple past, perfect and past continuous.
intro: The Odia past tense is refreshingly regular: add **-ଇଲି** for 'I', **-ଇଲା** for 'he/she', **-ଇଲେ** for respectful and plural subjects. If you know Hindi, there is a nice surprise: Odia has **no ergative construction** — the subject stays the subject and the verb agrees with it, even with transitive verbs (ମୁଁ ଭାତ ଖାଇଲି, not *mujh-ne*…).

vocab.note: ଗତ ସପ୍ତାହ 'last week', ଗତ ବର୍ଷ 'last year'.
ମୋର ଜନ୍ମ କଟକରେ 'I was born in Cuttack'.
ମୁଁ ଥିଲି, ତୁମେ ଥିଲ, ଆପଣ ଥିଲେ, ସେ ଥିଲା.

vocab.en: to be found, be available; to get

phrases.en: Have you eaten? (a common friendly greeting)

grammar.title: Simple past: -ଇଲି, -ଇଲା, -ଇଲେ (no ergative!)
grammar.body:
Add the past endings to the stem:
ମୁଁ ଦେଖିଲି *dekhili* — I saw
ଆମେ / ତୁ ଦେଖିଲୁ *dekhilu* — we / you (intimate) saw
ତୁମେ ଦେଖିଲ *dekhilô* — you (familiar) saw
ଆପଣ ଦେଖିଲେ *dekhile* — you (formal) saw
ସେ ଦେଖିଲା *dekhila* — he/she saw
ସେ / ସେମାନେ ଦେଖିଲେ *dekhile* — he/she (respectful) / they saw

**Irregular**: କରିବା → **କଲି, କଲା, କଲେ**; ଯିବା → **ଗଲି, ଗଲା, ଗଲେ**; ଦେବା → **ଦେଲି**; ନେବା → **ନେଲି**; ହେବା → **ହେଲି, ହେଲା**; ଅଛି → **ଥିଲି, ଥିଲା, ଥିଲେ** 'was'.

**No ergative**: unlike Hindi, Urdu, Punjabi or Marathi, Odia keeps the subject in its normal form and the verb agrees with *it*, whether the verb is transitive or not: ମୁଁ ଚିଠି ଲେଖିଲି 'I wrote a letter' — compare Hindi *maiṃne ciṭṭhī likhī*.

**Negative**: 'didn't' is usually the -ଇ form + ନାହିଁ (ମୁଁ ଯାଇ ନାହିଁ 'I didn't go / haven't gone'); the past + ନାହିଁ (ମୁଁ ଗଲି ନାହିଁ) is also heard, especially for a deliberate 'didn't'.

examples.en: I haven't had breakfast. / I didn't have breakfast.

grammar.title: Perfect, past perfect and past continuous
grammar.body:
**Present perfect -ଇଛି** — recent or relevant now: ମୁଁ ଖାଇଛି 'I have eaten', ସେ ଆସିଛନ୍ତି 'he/she has come'. Very common in conversation, often where English uses a simple past.

**Past perfect -ଇଥିଲି** — 'had done', also used for events in the more distant past: ମୁଁ ଗତ ବର୍ଷ କୋଣାର୍କ ଯାଇଥିଲି 'I went to Konark last year'.

**Past continuous -ଉଥିଲି** — 'was doing': ମୁଁ ପଢ଼ୁଥିଲି 'I was studying'; also 'used to': ପିଲାଦିନେ ମୁଁ ପୋଖରୀରେ ପହଁରୁଥିଲି 'as a child I used to swim in the pond'.

All take the usual person endings: -ଥିଲି, -ଥିଲୁ, -ଥିଲ, -ଥିଲେ, -ଥିଲା.

examples.en: I went to Konark last year.
At that time I was studying.

dialogue.title: A trip to Konark
dialogue.setting: On Monday, Lipi asks Sam about his weekend.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.en: Sam, what did you do on Saturday?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ମୁଁ ମୋ ସାଙ୍ଗମାନଙ୍କ ସହ କୋଣାର୍କ ଗଲି।
lines.roman: muṃ mo saṅgômanôṅkô sôhô Koṇarkô gôli.
lines.en: I went to Konark with my friends.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଅଦ୍ଭୁତ! ସୂର୍ଯ୍ୟ ମନ୍ଦିରର ଚକଗୁଡ଼ିକ ଦେଖି ମୁଁ ଆଶ୍ଚର୍ଯ୍ୟ ହୋଇଗଲି।
lines.roman: ôdbhutô! Surjyô Môndirôrô chôkôguṛikô dekhi muṃ aschôrjyô hoigôli.
lines.en: Amazing! I was astonished when I saw the wheels of the Sun Temple.

lines.speaker: Lipi
lines.en: Did you go to Chandrabhaga beach?

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ହଁ, କିନ୍ତୁ ସେଠି ଗୋଟିଏ ଘଟଣା ଘଟିଲା।
lines.roman: hôṃ, kintu seṭhi goṭie ghôṭôṇa ghôṭila.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ମୋ ଚପଲ ବାଲିରେ ହଜିଗଲା! ମୁଁ ଖାଲି ପାଦରେ ବସ୍ ଷ୍ଟାଣ୍ଡ ଯାଏ ଚାଲିଲି।
lines.roman: mo chôpôlô balire hôjigôla! muṃ khali padôre bôs sṭaṇḍ jae chalili.
lines.en: My sandals got lost in the sand! I walked barefoot all the way to the bus stand.

lines.speaker: Sam
lines.native: ଶେଷରେ ଗୋଟିଏ ଦୋକାନରୁ ନୂଆ ଚପଲ କିଣିଲି, ଆଉ ରାତି ଦଶଟାରେ ଘରେ ପହଞ୍ଚିଲି।
lines.roman: sesôre goṭie dokanôru nua chôpôlô kiṇili, au rati dôsôṭare ghôre pôhôñchili.
lines.en: In the end I bought new sandals at a shop and got home at ten at night.

culture: The 13th-century **Sun Temple at Konark** (a UNESCO World Heritage Site) is built as the Sun God's chariot, with 24 carved stone wheels that work as sundials; its wheel appears on Indian banknotes. Odisha's 'golden triangle' for visitors is Bhubaneswar (the 'temple city'), Puri and Konark.

tip.title: Was / were: ଥିଲି, ଥିଲା, ଥିଲେ
tip.body:
- The past of ଅଛି: ମୁଁ **ଥିଲି** · ଆମେ ଥିଲୁ · ତୁମେ **ଥିଲ** · ଆପଣ / ସେ (respectful) **ଥିଲେ** · ସେ / it **ଥିଲା**.
- 'Wasn't' is **ନ** + ଥିଲା: ସେ ଘରେ **ନଥିଲେ** 'he wasn't at home'.
- **ଗତ** = last: ଗତ ସପ୍ତାହ 'last week', ଗତ ବର୍ଷ 'last year'.

sentences.en: I was at the office yesterday.
Where were you last week?
I was little then.
He wasn't at home.

sentences.native: ଗତ ବର୍ଷ ପାଗ ବହୁତ ଗରମ ଥିଲା।
sentences.roman: gôtô bôrsô pagô bôhutô gôrômô thila.
sentences.en: The weather was very hot last year.
We were at the market then.
The train was two hours late.
My son was born in Puri.

tip.title: The simple past: -ଇଲି, -ଇଲା, -ଇଲେ
tip.body:
- Stem + **-ଇଲି** (I) · **-ଇଲୁ** (we) · **-ଇଲ** (you, friend) · **-ଇଲେ** (you polite; he/she respectful; they) · **-ଇଲା** (he/she, it).
- ଡାକିବା → ମୁଁ ଡାକିଲି, ବୋଉ ଡାକିଲେ.
- No ergative: the subject stays ମୁଁ, ସେ… and the verb agrees with it.

sentences.en: I got to the station at seven.
Mum called me.
Did you bring my book?
I sent Mum a photo.
He asked me my name.

sentences.native: ଶିକ୍ଷକ ପଚାରିଲେ, କିନ୍ତୁ କେହି ଉତ୍ତର ଦେଲେ ନାହିଁ।
sentences.roman: sikhyôkô pôcharile, kintu kehi uttôrô dele nahiṃ.
sentences.en: The teacher asked, but nobody answered.
Finally the bus came.
We got home at nine at night.

lessons.title: Went, did, gave: the irregular ones

tip.title: Irregular pasts
tip.body:
- ଯିବା → **ଗଲି, ଗଲା, ଗଲେ** (never ଯାଇଲି).
- କରିବା → **କଲି, କଲା, କଲେ** · ଦେବା → **ଦେଲି** · ନେବା → **ନେଲି** · ହେବା → **ହେଲା**.
- Start and finish use ହେଲା: ଆରମ୍ଭ **ହେଲା** 'it started', ଶେଷ **ହେଲା** 'it ended'.

sentences.en: I went to the market yesterday.
What did you do yesterday evening?
The meeting started at ten.
When did the film finish?

sentences.native: ମୁଁ ତାଙ୍କୁ ଦୁଇ ଶହ ଟଙ୍କା ଦେଲି।
sentences.roman: muṃ taṅku dui sôhô ṭôṅka deli.
sentences.en: I gave him two hundred rupees.
Dad went to the office in the morning.
We took an auto.
I left the key at home.
She quit her job.

lessons.title: Have you eaten? I've been there

tip.title: Have done, had done, was doing
tip.body:
- **-ଇଛି** 'have done' — recent or still relevant: ମୁଁ ଖାଇଛି 'I've eaten'.
- **-ଇଥିଲି** 'did / had done' — further back: ମୁଁ ଥରେ ଯାଇଥିଲି 'I went once'.
- **-ଉଥିଲି** 'was doing' or 'used to': ମୁଁ ରାନ୍ଧୁଥିଲି.
- **ଖାଇଛ?** 'Have you eaten?' is a friendly hello.

sentences.en: I've just eaten — I'm not hungry.
Have you been to Puri before?
Yes, I went once.
Has Dad come back from the office?
I've forgotten her name.
I was cooking at the time.
I used to walk every day.
I've seen this film before.

sentences.native: ହଁ, ଏବେ ମୋର ମନେପଡ଼ିଲା, ତାଙ୍କ ନାମ ଲିପି।
sentences.roman: hôṃ, ebe morô mônepôṛila, taṅkô namô Lipi.
sentences.en: Yes, now I remember — her name is Lipi.

tip.title: It got lost vs I lost it
tip.body:
- **-ଇଗଲା** = it happened (by itself): ମୋ ଚାବି **ହଜିଗଲା** 'my key got lost'.
- **-ଇଦେଲି** = I did it: ମୁଁ ଚାବି **ହଜାଇଦେଲି** 'I lost the key'.
- 'I found it': ମିଳିଲା — ମୋତେ ଚାବି ମିଳିଲା.

sentences.en: My key's gone missing.
I lost my bag on the bus.

sentences.native: ଶେଷରେ ଫୋନ ମିଳିଲା, ଖଟ ତଳେ ଥିଲା!
sentences.roman: sesôre phonô miḷila, khôṭô tôḷe thila!
sentences.en: I finally found the phone — it was under the bed!
The child got lost in the market.
Did you get the tickets?
Suddenly the power went off.
Something happened on the road yesterday.
Suddenly my friend turned up.
Who won the match yesterday?

sentences.native: ଆମେ ହାରିଗଲୁ, କିନ୍ତୁ ଖେଳ ବହୁତ ଭଲ ଥିଲା।
sentences.roman: ame harigôlu, kintu kheḷô bôhutô bhôlô thila.
sentences.en: We lost, but it was a great match.
India lost the last match.
You won! Brilliant!

sentences.native: ମୋ ଭାଇର ବିବାହ ଗତ ମାସରେ ହେଲା।
sentences.roman: mo bhairô bibahô gôtô masôre hela.
sentences.en: My brother got married last month.
Lots of people came to the wedding.
We watched the match till late at night.
Back then we used to play together every day.
